title: Image token requests can run in parallel
summary:
Image token requests gained room to run in parallel, while shared queues brought text and image concurrency rules together.

Image requests made with a token are no longer restricted to one at a time. Anonymous requests retain a concurrency cap of one.

Concurrency caps now sit in a shared IP queue: seed allows 3 requests, flower 10, and nectar 30. Nectar requests use the queue rather than bypassing it; text token requests keep their one-second queue interval, while image token requests have no interval. Token and referrer lookups are cached for 30 seconds.

Websim’s worker now sends a Bearer token to the text API when configured and continues without one otherwise. Its code also moved to a top-level repository directory.
